articles.title: Let’s Encrypt Cuts Default Certificate Validity to 64 Days Ahead of 45-Day Switch
articles.summary:
Open Certificate Authority (CA) Let’s Encrypt is taking the first step towards reducing the validity period of the certificates it issues.
Beginning February 10, 2027, it will issue certificates with 64-day lifetimes by default, in preparation for 45-day lifetimes planned for 2028.
In line with the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, the shorter certificate validity period is expected to improve security on the web by making revocation more efficient and limiting the scope of compromise.
All publicly trusted CAs will make similar changes, Let’s Encrypt noted in a December 2025 blog, when it revealed the planned timeline for switching to 45-day certificates.
Last week, the CA announced that, after February 10, 2027, all newly issued or renewed certificates will have a 64-day validity period, with the last 90-day certificate expected to expire on May 11, 2027.
This week, Let’s Encrypt will start issuing 64-day certificates in its staging environment for testing purposes, and recommends that all customers perform similar tests before the change enters production.
“If your renewals are automated and your client supports ACME Renewal Info (ARI), you should be all set since ARI allows Let’s Encrypt to tell your client when to renew (you can review your ACME client’s documentation to determine if ARI is implemented),” Let’s Encrypt notes.

articles.title: Run multi-node inference workloads using Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Run multi-node inference workloads using Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers
This post shows how to deploy one large language model (LLM) across two GPU nodes on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the multi-node Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers. It uses separate prefill and decode nodes behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This kind of multi-node setup is common for tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, as well as prefill/decode disaggregation inference workloads. In a previous post, we introduced the Ray Serve DLC and used it to stand up a small model behind an HTTP endpoint on a single GPU node. You had a working inference endpoint, and the container keeps the GPU stack compatible, including CUDA libraries, so you did not need to write boilerplate code.
Ray is a distributed compute framework, so Ray Serve deployments can span multiple nodes. Customers use multi-node Ray Serve for several reasons. Some want to run foundation or open-weight models that are too large for a single GPU. Others need more throughput than one replica can deliver. Still others want to separate the two phases of inference to improve performance. In each case, customers must build the dependency chain themselves: choosing compatible libraries for the GPU stack and debugging issues when a component drifts out of alignment. This is undifferentiated work that takes time and effort away from delivering models.

articles.summary:
This week, we’re talking with Canada’s newest fintech unicorn, Koho.
Earlier this year, Koho raised $130 million CAD as part of its quest to move from challenger bank to an actual bank.
“I think that we will look back on prediction markets the same way we look back on altcoins and … NFTs.”
The company is nearing the end of its 5-year journey to secure a Schedule 1 banking licence, which CEO Daniel Eberhard claims will help Koho offer more competitive lending and savings rates to everyday Canadians.

And this convo is wide-ranging, covering the increasing amount of international competition flooding into the Canadian financial space, the lack of participation in new payments infrastructure from the Big Six banks, and all the new features Koho has launched or plans to launch in its ever-expanding portfolio—including maybe a Koho telco?
We also talked about one feature Koho does not plan to launch: prediction markets.

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows 11 23H2 reaches end of support in 30 days
articles.summary:
Microsoft has reminded customers that systems running Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions will stop receiving security updates next month.
The announcement follows the end of support for Windows 11 23H2 Home and Pro editions in November 2025.
Users are now advised to upgrade to Windows 11 26H2 (also known as the Windows 11 2026 Update), which became generally available in September 2026 as an enablement package (eKB) and will reach end of support for consumers in October 2029.
"The November 2026 Windows security update will be the last update available for these editions. After this date, devices running these editions will no longer receive monthly security updates containing protections from the latest security threats," it said in a message center update. "We recommend updating eligible devices running Windows 11, version 23H2 to a supported version of Windows 11."
Windows 11 26H2 is now available in a phased rollout to eligible Windows 11 devices for those who have enabled the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" setting.
"If the update is ready for your device, it will download and install automatically, and a single restart will complete the process," Microsoft added.
You can also manually check if the update is available by clicking "Check for updates" in the Settings > Windows Update section. If the system is ready to update, you'll see the option to "Download and install Windows 11, version 26H2."

Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
Logpush delivers logs in batches as quickly as possible, enabling Cloudflare to provide information almost in real time. During our recent Birthday Week, we made Logpush available on all self-serve plans and Transformers generally available.
Those changes were among eight major updates to Cloudflare Observability and reflect our commitment to make every Cloudflare feature available to everyone. This post takes a deeper look at how Transformers work inside Logpush's export pipeline. Observability teams use Logpush to export Cloudflare logs to security information and event management systems (SIEMs), analytics platforms, and object storage. Before those logs reach their destination, teams may need to remove health checks, omit sensitive fields, or reshape records for dashboards and investigations. Today, this often requires a separate processing service that teams must deploy, scale, monitor, and maintain.
For example, a team that collects logs from multiple CDNs can add a static provider field to normalize records before they reach its analytics platform. articles.title: Ledger confirme un implant espion dans un portefeuille vendu par son propre revendeur agréé — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Ledger, le fabricant français qui domine le marché des portefeuilles physiques pour cryptomonnaies, a dû admettre ce que ses clients redoutent le plus.
Dans un message publié sur X le samedi 10 octobre, son support explique que l’appareil d’une victime contenait « un implant matériel non autorisé ». Toutes les victimes connues avaient acheté leur portefeuille chez CryptoBilis, un revendeur agréé présent en Indonésie, en Malaisie et aux Philippines.
Des chercheurs qui suivent les transactions sur la blockchain estiment que 86 à 93 millions de dollars ont été volés, soit environ 77 à 83 millions d’euros, dans plus de 300 portefeuilles, d’après CoinDesk. De son côté, Ledger n’a confirmé aucun montant. La marque juge « limité » le nombre d’appareils touchés.
Ce type d’appareil sert justement à empêcher ce genre de vol. Un portefeuille physique ressemble à une clé USB et garde hors ligne les clés privées, ces codes secrets qui permettent de dépenser des cryptomonnaies. À la première mise en route, il affiche une phrase de récupération de 24 mots. Toute personne qui connaît ces mots a accès aux fonds.
Un mouchard qui passe le contrôle d’authenticité
Ledger n’a pas décrit l’implant. Mark Karpelès, l’ancien patron de Mt.Gox (la plateforme d’échange de bitcoins qui a fait faillite en 2014), a publié sur X des photos d’un Ledger Nano X démonté qui contient un composant suspect. D’après son analyse, ce composant lit les données envoyées à l’écran et transmet les 24 mots vers l’extérieur…

articles.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise
Institutions are recalculating who controls the technology they rely on. Mozilla has an independent option to offer.
For years, organizations consolidated technology around a small number of providers to make things simpler. Fewer systems. Tighter integrations. More economies of scale. But that consolidation went well beyond technology. It consolidated dependency, too. The resulting risks have been debated, studied, and challenged along the way, but concentration continued. More work, data and critical infrastructure kept moving to the same few providers, while credible alternatives narrowed.
The deeper that dependency runs, the harder and more costly it becomes to change course. When something fails, changes or falls outside an institution’s control, that dependency becomes a risk for CIOs and CISOs to manage.
Nowhere are these stakes more visible than in Europe. Now institutions are re-assessing. Governments are pushing for greater digital autonomy, while regulated industries face growing pressure to find and manage their dependencies.
There’s a name for much of this debate about technological control: “sovereignty.”
What digital sovereignty means in practice varies. Across Europe, governments are investing in the security and resilience of critical IT infrastructure, reducing strategic dependencies and putting technological autonomy higher on national agendas. articles.summary:
TeraLumen Solutions is building India’s terahertz industry from the ground up
With four patents, commercialised products, and clinical trials under way, TeraLumen Solutions is proving that world‑class terahertz systems can be made in India.
For years, terahertz technology remained largely confined to research laboratories because the equipment needed to work with it was expensive and difficult to source. For Jyotirmayee Dash, Founder, CEO and Managing Director of Chennai-based TeraLumen Solutions, that limitation became the reason to build a company.
Dash encountered the technology during her PhD, when the terahertz devices she used were imported, often at an exorbitant price.
“Most of the devices I was using during my doctoral degree were being imported from Germany and the US, with the cost close to Rs 1.1 crore,” Dash says. “With that in mind, after my degree, I thought, why can't we make it here?”
Founded in 2019, TeraLumen initially focused on using terahertz technology for cancer-margin detection, partly inspired by a close friend's cancer diagnosis. It has since expanded into industrial inspection and research equipment.
The company now has 25 employees and manufactures its own hardware and software. Its products include TeraXPLOR, a research and spectroscopy system; TeraNIM, a non-destructive testing platform for industries such as aerospace, automotive, and oil and gas; and TeraMargin, its cancer-margin detection technology. articles.title: Quand l'IA disparaît, les résultats s'effondrent : ce que révèle une étude sur ChatGPT et la persévérance
articles.summary:
Comment réagit notre cerveau face à l’intelligence artificielle (IA) ? La question se pose alors que cette technologie promet de nous faciliter le quotidien en nous assistant dans nos recherches, nos écrits, et diverses interrogations. Dans une étude portant sur 1 222 participants, on apprend qu’utiliser une IA plus de 10 minutes pourrait justement nous faire perdre une faculté : celle de persévérer face à un problème.
Le papier est signé par cinq chercheurs, dont Grace Liu (université Carnegie Mellon), première autrice, et Brian Christian, chercheur à l’université d’Oxford, auteur de The Alignment Problem (2020), qui réfléchit aux effets de l’IA sur nos esprits depuis une vingtaine d’années.
L’étude a été présentée à San Francisco lors de la Conference on Language Modeling (COLM), qui s’est tenue du 6 au 9 octobre. Pour y être acceptée, elle a été relue par des spécialistes extérieurs à l’équipe, ce qu’on appelle la relecture par les pairs (peer review). Elle est disponible dans la forme présentée lors de la conférence via le serveur arXiv.

Dans un premier temps, les auteurs ont recruté 354 personnes à travers les États-Unis pour leur demander de résoudre 15 calculs de fractions, de plus en plus difficiles, en une quinzaine de minutes. articles.title: Critical SonicWall Vulnerability Exploited Days After Disclosure
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances within days after public disclosure.
Tracked as CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS score of 10), the security defect is described as a pre-authenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) issue affecting the SMA1000 Work Place interface.
According to SonicWall, an unintended alternate access path could allow a remote attacker “to direct the appliance to issue requests on their behalf and reach internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations.”
The company disclosed CVE-2026-102255 on October 6, urging customers to update their 6210, 7210, and 8200v models to software versions 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670.
On Friday, threat intelligence firms Previdian (formerly KEVIntel) and Defused warned of the first exploitation attempts targeting the security bug.
Defused said that the first exploitation attempts reached its SMA decoys on October 8, only two days after public disclosure.
“SonicWall SMA1000 exploitation attempts are now being observed by Previdian sensors, consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10.0). The vulnerability allows unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF),” Previdian said.
Successful exploitation of the flaw could allow attackers to take over vulnerable devices, cybersecurity firm Horizon3.ai warned.

Cette fois, l’équipe a nettement pris de l’avance sur ses cycles précédents. Elle y arrive alors que Google verrouille de plus en plus le code source d’Android, sur lequel tout le projet repose.
Des applications maison enfin soignées

articles.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
articles.summary:
GitLab warned users today to immediately patch a maximum-severity vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle and reported via GitLab's HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness in GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in projects' pipeline configuration files.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained in a Monday advisory.
GitLab fixed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.4, and 19.4 before 19.4.2, and urged users to patch their servers immediately.
"These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately," it warned. "GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action."
CVE-2026-97229 is the latest in a string of vulnerabilities that GitLab has addressed…

articles.title: Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders
articles.summary:
CXL has seen a massive surge recently, and Marvell announced its second-generation Structera X CXL memory expanders, adding CXL 3.2 support, PCIe Gen6 connectivity, and increasing memory channels from four to six. For hyperscalers running DDR4 and lower-speed DDR5 reclamation projects, that means the DDR4 version can support up to 18 DDR4 RDIMMs.
Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders
Patrick gave us the decoder for the models:
- CXL 3 support is indicated by the first digit 3, just as the 2 in last year’s 2404 and 2504 marked CXL 2.0.
- 5 or 4, is the DDR generation
- The trailing two digits are the memory channel count.
Structera X 3406 is therefore a CXL 3 DDR4 part with six channels, while the 3506 is the CXL 3 DDR5 part, also at six channels. This announcement covers only the Structera X memory expansion line, not the Structera A near-memory compute controller that Marvell showed us last year. Still, CXL is focused on optimizing either bandwidth per core (since CXL bandwidth is in addition to native DDR bandwidth) and also capacity expansion.
PCIe Gen6 infrastructure and CXL 3.2 means we get roughly twice the bandwidth over the link, so that is how Marvell is adding more bandwidth from more memory channels.
Both new controllers stay on Marvell’s 5nm process and have LZ4 compression. Compression means the installed memory is storing more than the physical DRAM capacity. In this generation, Marvell is ensuring that the LZ4 can keep up with the interface…

SpaceFields is turning solid propulsion R&D into scaled manufacturing
From winning iDEX challenges to signing MoUs with defence PSUs, IISc-incubated SpaceFields is moving from bespoke propulsion design to large‑scale supply.

articles.title: Test de Valor Mortis, le mariage parfait entre Dark Souls et FPS
articles.summary:
Sur le papier, Valor Mortis ressemble à un immense pari. One More Level, spécialiste de la vue à la première personne appliquée à des genres qui ne s’y prêtent pas forcément, a décidé de se frotter aux soulslike, façon FPS, donc. Le studio entend garantir la même exigence en termes de gameplay, mais avec une immersion au plus près des combats, quand les autres héritiers de la trilogie Dark Souls conservent cette vue à la troisième personne permettant de mieux appréhender les dangers.
En somme, One More Level n’a pas voulu se renier avec Valor Mortis, alors qu’il aurait pu abandonner son savoir-faire au profit de la logique et, pourrait-on le penser, d’une certaine forme de bon sens. Le risque est réel, mais on est ravi de constater, après une quinzaine d’heures de jeu, que Valor Mortis est une expérience globalement réussie.
Points forts
- Une bonne proposition dans le genre soulslike
- Un vrai sens de la progression
- Univers soigné, narration immersive
Points faibles
- Quelques animations à revoir chez les ennemis
- Les chiens et les moustiques
- Quelques boss décevants
Valor Mortis est un savant mélange, avec un gameplay aux petits oignons

The Fitbit Edge is for folks who don’t want to go totally screenless
A middle-of-the-road option that combines the Air’s simplicity with some of the Pixel Watch’s smarts.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
articles.summary:
GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
Learn how to add custom instructions and skills to your repository, use custom agents, and connect MCP servers like Playwright.
Context matters when you’re working with AI. Every codebase has its own house rules: how components are structured, which scripts to run, and which conventions apply to different frameworks and file types.
Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too. Much of that knowledge can live inside the repository, so Copilot can pick it up automatically instead of requiring you to explain the same standards, scripts, and workflows every time you start a new task.
In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project:
- Custom instructions communicate the conventions Copilot should follow.
- Agent skills package repeatable procedures.
- Custom agents bring specialized guidance to larger tasks.
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers connect Copilot to external tools and data sources, expanding what it can do.
Let’s look at how each one works and how they can work together.
Start with custom instructions
Suppose you ask Copilot to add a custom page size to an application. Making the change is only part of the job. The new code should also follow the patterns your team already uses.

articles.title: NASA vai investigar buraco na Lua que pode levar a uma caverna
articles.summary:
A NASA selecionou uma missão para investigar uma abertura na superfície da Lua que pode dar acesso a uma estrutura subterrânea maior. O projeto, chamado Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation (GIMLI), pretende estudar o poço Marius Hills Pit (MHP) diretamente no solo lunar, para determinar se ele se conecta a uma caverna formada por antigas atividades vulcânicas.
Localizado em uma região com histórico de atividade vulcânica, o buraco tem dimensões estimadas de até 150 pés (cerca de 46 metros) de profundidade e 300 pés (cerca de 91 metros) de largura. Cientistas acreditam que a formação pode ser uma abertura causada pelo desabamento do teto de um tubo de lava subterrâneo, estrutura que também pode ajudar a explicar a história geológica da Lua.
Como será a investigação da NASA
Até agora, o Marius Hills Pit foi estudado apenas por observações feitas a partir da órbita lunar. A missão GIMLI pretende avançar nessa investigação com o uso de um veículo robótico equipado com instrumentos especializados para analisar as características do terreno e identificar possíveis estruturas abaixo da superfície.
Entre os equipamentos previstos estão um radar de penetração no solo, sondas sísmicas e um gravímetro, sensor que mede a intensidade do campo gravitacional. O rover também contará com câmeras para registrar imagens das partes expostas do poço.

articles.summary:
A Canada-based cybersecurity expert was arrested last week in the United States on suspicion of being involved in ShinyHunters attacks, including the recent hacking of FBI systems.
FBI director Kash Patel announced on Friday that agents had arrested another suspected ShinyHunters co-conspirator.
“This is the latest arrest this FBI has made in a matter of days involving this network, as we work non-stop to dismantle the group, pursue new leads and evidence, and act quickly,” Patel stated, adding, “We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate.”
The suspect has not officially been named, but The New York Times and cybersecurity blogger Brian Krebs reported that he is Edward Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity expert specializing in ransomware response.
The Royal Canadian Mounted Police confirmed for CBS News that it’s aware of the arrest of a Canadian in the United States in connection with ShinyHunters.
Dubrovsky was reportedly arrested by the FBI after traveling to Philadelphia for a conference. He is suspected of being involved in the recent ShinyHunters attack targeting the FBI.

articles.title: El ex de Hayden Panettiere pide al tribunal que actúe como representante de su hija para proteger la herencia
articles.summary:
Wladimir Klitschko ya tiene la custodia de su hija Kaya, pero eso no le da ningún poder sobre lo que la niña hereda de su madre. Por eso ha ido al tribunal de sucesiones del condado de Los Ángeles: pide que lo nombren tutor temporal de su patrimonio. El escrito se presentó el jueves 24 de septiembre y la vista está señalada para hoy.
Hayden Panettiere murió el 16 de agosto, a los 36 años, en un apartamento de Greenville, en Carolina del Sur. El forense del condado habló de una sobredosis accidental de varias sustancias, entre ellas fentanilo; la policía de la ciudad investiga y, según lo publicado, la DEA se habría sumado a la investigación. Kaya es, según el escrito, su única heredera.
Tiene la custodia, ¿para qué quiere una tutela?
Son dos cosas distintas. Por un lado, la custodia decide dónde vive la niña y quién la cuida. Lo que es la tutela del patrimonio decide quién firma por ella cuando hay dinero de por medio, porque, como es normal, una menor no puede administrarlos.
En el primer caso, Klitschko decide el colegio; para firmar en su nombre un papel del banco, necesita otro tipo de autorización.
Por eso mismo, Klitschko pide ser tutor temporal, no definitivo, y el escrito define la medida como “urgent and essential”. Lo que dice buscar es proteger lo que hereda Kaya hasta que el tribunal designe a alguien que administre el patrimonio de la actriz, y según la petición, también quiere estar legitimado para impulsar ese nombramiento.

articles.title: Linus Torvalds, qui réduisait l’IA à « 90 % de marketing », publie un patch du noyau Linux écrit avec Claude Code — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Le nom de la branche ne laisse aucun doute : noref-filemap-read-with-llm. Le suffixe signifie « avec un LLM », c’est-à-dire un grand modèle de langage. Michael Larabel, fondateur de Phoronix, un site spécialisé dans Linux, l’a repérée le 11 octobre dans le dépôt personnel de Linus Torvalds, créateur et mainteneur en chef du noyau. Dans le message qui accompagne les patchs, Linus Torvalds explique que le code, les programmes de test, la revue et le premier jet du texte ont été faits « avec un assistant de code IA (Claude Code) sous ma direction ».
Les mesures de performance, elles, ont été lancées par Linus Torvalds sur sa propre machine (il n’a donc pas confié le chronomètre à l’IA). Le noyau Linux fait tourner la plupart des serveurs du web et tous les smartphones Android. Chaque modification y passe par une revue réputée impitoyable. Avec ce patch, les opposants au code généré par IA perdent un allié de poids.
De « 90 % de marketing » à Claude Code dans le noyau
En octobre 2024, interrogé par TFiR à l’Open Source Summit de Vienne, Linus Torvalds résumait l’industrie de l’IA à « 90 % de marketing et 10 % de réalité ». Il disait alors l’ignorer, faute de supporter l’emballement autour du sujet. Plus tard, il s’en est aussi pris aux rapports de bugs générés par IA qui encombrent les mainteneurs.

articles.title: Fervo’s Utah Geothermal Plant Starts Sending Clean Power To The Grid
articles.summary:
This article was originally published by Canary Media.
The geothermal startup Fervo Energy is now selling power to the grid from its Cape Station project in Utah — marking the first time a utility-scale, next-generation geothermal facility has achieved such a feat worldwide.
The Houston-based firm turned on an initial 33-megawatt unit late last week and has been testing and ramping up output since then. On Thursday, Fervo will officially begin commercial operations, supplying carbon-free electricity to Shell Energy, a retail power provider in California.
Cape Station, a $2 billion project that will eventually be 500 MW, is unique among the world’s commercial geothermal plants. While other facilities draw on naturally occurring hot water and steam, Fervo has engineered its own geothermal resource deep underground. The startup uses drilling techniques from the oil and gas industry to create reservoirs in hot, dry rocks that generate steam to produce electricity.
“Traditional geothermal would have never been done in southern Utah,” says Dawn Owens, Fervo’s senior vice president and head of development and commercial markets.
With the first unit online, Fervo says it is working to commission two more 33-MW power blocks by 1 January, 2027. The project’s remaining 400 MW — which is supported by a new agreement with Google — is under construction and slated to come online in 2028.

articles.title: ReplaySSM: Rethinking State Storage for Faster Hybrid-Model Decoding | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Hybrid models interleave state-space model (SSM) layers with a few attention layers. NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3-Flash are all built this way, with Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet (GDN), or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) as the SSM layer.
SSM layers are designed to make decoding fast: they use a fixed-size state in place of a key-value (KV) cache that grows with context length. At serving batch sizes, however, the SSM layers, not attention, can be the latency bottleneck up to 100K tokens of context. SSM layers also complicate two techniques that reliably speed up attention decoding: speculative decoding and quantization.
ReplaySSM makes SSM layers the fast part again. It represents the SSM state as a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs. This separates output computation from state updates and addresses three challenges in current SSM decoding: state traffic, rollback for speculative decoding, and error accumulation in a quantized state.
ReplaySSM is joint work between NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton. The paper, ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State, details all three benefits and presents the full evaluation. It is available on arXiv, with code on GitHub. It is integrated into NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and FlashInfer, and also runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3.

articles.title: Microsoft intègre les applis Office directement dans Copilot
articles.summary:
Après avoir intégré Copilot dans les différentes applications de sa suite bureautique Office, Microsoft est partie pour faire l’inverse. La firme de Redmond vient en effet d’annoncer qu’elle allait intégrer Office dans sa nouvelle application Microsoft Copilot. Avec cette manœuvre, les utilisateurs pourront profiter de l’ensemble des fonctionnalités de la suite Microsoft 365 au cœur d’une expérience de travail gérée par l’IA.
Une expérience unifiée pour faire travailler l’IA à votre place
Les fonctions de création et de collaboration de Word, Excel et PowerPoint vont officiellement intégrer la nouvelle application Copilot de Microsoft. Concrètement, cette intégration doit vous permettre de passer d’un prompt initial à un document, un tableur ou une présentation finale, sans rupture. Vous pouvez commencer directement dans le chat Copilot ou dans Cowork, et continuer dans les applications Office autonomes.
En fonction des tâches à réaliser, vous pourrez en outre sélectionner le modèle d’IA le plus adapté, ou laisser Copilot choisir automatiquement pour vous le meilleur modèle.

articles.title: Retail giant Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack
articles.summary:
Retail giant Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail chains, confirmed today that it was forced to take some systems offline after a "cybersecurity incident."
As a wholesale company and multinational retailer, Ahold Delhaize operates more than 9,400 local stores across Europe, the United States, and Indonesia, employs nearly 400,000 people, and serves around 60 million customers each week through physical retail locations and online.
Ahold Delhaize reported yearly net sales of over $104 billion in 2024, and it owns a wide range of brands, including Delhaize, Maxi, Mega Image, Albert, bol, Alfa Beta, Etos, Gall & Gall, and Profi in Europe, and Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, and Hannaford in the American market.
In a succinct press release published earlier today, the company added that it's working to mitigate the incident and that its stores are open to customers.
"Ahold Delhaize is experiencing a security issue within its network. Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue. This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them. At this time, our stores are open and serving customers," it said.
"Protecting our infrastructure in the best interest of our customers, associates and partners is a top priority. We apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused customers and partners."

articles.title: Nintendo 3DS : cette application inattendue lui permet de faire tourner vos jeux PC récents
articles.summary:
Six ans après l’arrêt de sa production, la Nintendo New 3DS trouve une seconde jeunesse grâce à Kasumi. Ce client non officiel permet de jouer à des titres PC récents via GeForce Now ou de diffuser les jeux de son propre ordinateur avec Steam Link.
Nintendo a cessé de produire la 3DS en septembre 2020, mais certains développeurs refusent visiblement de la laisser prendre la poussière. Avec Kasumi, publié sur GitHub par p0mpurin, une New 3DS modifiée peut désormais servir d’écran et de manette pour des jeux exécutés à distance.
La console ne fait évidemment pas tourner ces titres elle-même. GeForce Now s’occupe des calculs dans le cloud, puis lui envoie l’image et le son tandis que Kasumi transmet les commandes. L’application exploite au passage toute la largeur de l’écran supérieur, qui affiche une définition de 800 points par 240, soit 400×240 pixels par œil lorsque la 3D est utilisée.
Une New 3DS modifiée suffit pour se lancer
Le fonctionnement reprend celui de n’importe quel service de cloud gaming. L’utilisateur choisit un jeu compatible qu’il possède notamment sur Steam, Epic Games Store ou Ubisoft Connect, puis celui-ci est exécuté sur les serveurs de NVIDIA.
La connexion au compte passe par un code affiché sur la console et saisi depuis un téléphone ou un ordinateur. Aucun mot de passe NVIDIA ne transite ainsi directement par la 3DS.
Kasumi reste toutefois un homebrew et nécessite donc une console modifiée, par exemple avec Luma3DS. La 3DS originale n’est pas compatibl…

articles.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
articles.summary:
At a glance
- StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutors before they are tested with real learners; it is not a product, is not deployed in classrooms, and is not intended to replace teachers
- AI tutoring tools need feedback from students to improve, but collecting that feedback through human studies is slow, costly, and difficult to scale
- StudentSim trains personalized AI student simulators from publicly available, de-identified learner records, with one simulator adapted to each student
- The work evaluates simulators along two education-grounded dimensions: whether they respond like a specific student, and whether they update after tutor guidance
- Across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics, StudentSim outperforms leading baselines and provides a useful feedback signal for training an AI tutor
In research settings, teams are exploring how AI-powered tutoring systems can help explain a math problem, suggest an edit to a writing assignment, or guide a learner through a chess position. Yet the quality of teaching cannot be measured only from the tutor’s answer. A tutor needs to know what happens after the guidance reaches a student. Did the student correct the original mistake? Did the hint help them reason toward the answer, or did it give away too much? Would a different student need a different kind of support? articles.title: Bilder, Videos, Audioaufnahmen: Nasa veröffentlicht 800 Gigabyte Daten von der Artemis-2-Mission
articles.summary:
Artemis-2-Mission: Nasa veröffentlicht 800 Gigabyte Daten für alle
Die Artemis-2-Mission der Nasa war eine besondere. Sie startete Anfang April vom Cape Canaveral und umrundete nach fünf Tagen den Mond. Nach insgesamt neuntägigem Flug landete die Orion-Kapsel im Pazifik.
Dabei handelte es sich um den ersten bemannten Flug zum Mond seit der Apollo-17-Mission im Jahr 1972. Die Artemis-2-Mission diente als Testflug, um Lebenserhaltungssysteme, Navigation und das Orion-Raumschiff unter Realbedingungen im tiefen Weltraum zu prüfen. Auf dem Mond selbst landeten de Astronauten dabei alleri
Auch bisher unveröffentlichtes Material ist unter den Daten
Im Laufe der Mission entstanden viele Aufnahmen und wissenschaftliche Beobachtungen – und diese werden in dieser Woche der Öffentlichkeit zur Verfügung gestellt. Am Mittwoch werde der „vollständige Datensatz […] für weitere Analysen“ veröffentlicht, teilte die Nasa in einer Pressemitteilung mit.
Mehr als 800 Gigabyte an wissenschaftlichen Monddaten der Artemis-II-Mission – darunter auch bisher unveröffentlichtes Material – seien in das „Planetary Data System“, das öffentliche Archiv für die Planetenmissionen der Nasa, hochgeladen worden, hieß es in der Pressemitteilung.

articles.title: How CaliperAI is building modular robots for industrial inspection
articles.summary:
How CaliperAI is building modular robots for industrial inspection
Bengaluru-based startup CaliperAI is developing software for physical AI and configurable robotic platforms that can be adapted for different industrial applications.
A robot inspecting an electrical substation cannot afford to miss a fault, just as an autonomous vehicle cannot afford to overlook an unexpected obstacle. Building machines that can operate reliably in such environments requires data, software, testing infrastructure, and hardware that help them interpret the physical world.
Bengaluru-based CaliperAI is developing this infrastructure alongside its own modular robotic platforms.
Founded in 2024 by Mohanvarakrishna Boddeti and Gautham Raju, the startup initially focused on gaps in autonomous-driving software development and validation before expanding into physical AI and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) for inspecting heavy industrial assets.
The founders spent six to eight months validating the idea before leaving their jobs to work full-time on the startup in May 2025. CaliperAI currently has a team of eight.
The company’s name reflects its focus on precision.
“We wanted to develop AI which works as precisely as measuring with calipers,” says Co-founder Gautham Raju. “While AI can go wrong anytime, we want to be extremely precise in the AI we develop."

articles.title: Google lance un nouveau bracelet pour suivre sa santé, cette fois-ci avec un écran
articles.summary:
Lancé en mai 2026, le Google Fitbit Air rencontre un grand succès. Il faut dire que la proposition de Google à 99 euros est très alléchante : ce bracelet sans écran, léger et endurant, mesure la santé et le sport et permet de se passer d’une montre connectée. Mais le produit a néanmoins quelques lacunes liées à sa nature : il est totalement passif. On le porte sans savoir ce qu’il enregistre, ce qui peut créer quelques déceptions. Dans notre test, nous déplorions de devoir sortir notre téléphone pour enregistrer certaines séances de sport, au risque de ne pas du tout avoir les bonnes informations.

Ce successeur des bracelets Fitbit Charge, le premier sous la marque Google, est la preuve que l’ambition santé du géant du web ne s’arrête pas au premier essai. Il coûte 179,99 euros, ce qui le place entre le Fitbit Air et une Pixel Watch.
À quoi sert l’écran du Google Fitbit Edge ?

articles.title: Apollyon Dynamics quits building drones to make defencetech for the military
articles.summary:
Apollyon Dynamics quits building drones to make defencetech for the military
Hyderabad-based student startup Apollyon Dynamics sold drones worth over Rs 1.5 crore last year. It has now moved to a jet-powered target drone, a multirotor interceptor, and a marine unmanned system.
When Jayant Khatri and Sourya Choudhury started in May 2025, the focus of the Hyderabad-based defencetech startup was building drones. Its early portfolio included trainer, endurance, multirole, and FPV systems, with the company selling drones worth more than Rs 1.5 crore last year.
But foresight prevails over immediate success. Anticipating saturation in the market, Apollyon has now pivoted.
“We have stopped building regular drones. Instead, we have completely shifted towards making higher value products,” says Khatri, Co-founder and CEO of Apollyon Dynamics.
The founder says the conventional drone market had become too crowded, with limited room for differentiation. “It’s basically a race to the bottom now. People are just assembling stuff. That included us as well. There’s not a lot of value addition,” he says.
The startup’s current portfolio has been rebuilt around three core products: Nightshade, Ahuti Mk II, and Project Piranha.
Apollyon now has around 20 full-time employees, two manufacturing labs, and an office in Hyderabad.

If you’ve delved into the worlds of Star Trek, The Terminator or William Gibson’s cyberpunk novel Neuromancer, you’ll know that enhanced, electronic vision is a staple of science fiction. Now, what was once futuristic fiction is becoming a reality.
Researchers have developed bionic eyes that can restore some lost vision. These devices’ capabilities are currently basic, but they have been steadily improving in recent years.
One day, they might even offer features that transcend the limits of natural human eyesight – for instance by manipulating images in a way the human eye cannot or by seeing beyond the spectrum of visible light.
Technology that boosts people’s physical and mental abilities is no longer the preserve of science fiction. In this series, we explore cutting-edge ways that human capabilities could be augmented both now and in the near future – and the ethics of these innovations.
To date, implants have focused on combatting problems with the retina, the light-sensing layer of cells inside the back of the eye. Akin to the film in the back of a camera, the retina allows us to see the outside world. When things go badly wrong with it, the result can be a total loss of vision.

Most of the Macs are from 2012, but together they have reached a reported 1.3 teraflops in matrix-multiplication tests. Visitors can watch calculations run on a single core before seeing the workload distributed across the cluster.
The Museo de Historia de la Computación spent 18 months developing the exhibit. The replica preserves the appearance of the 1976 machine without trying to reproduce its internal hardware. Built to mark the 50th anniversaries of the Cray-1 and Apple's founding, the model is now on permanent display at the museum alongside two unused authentic Cray CX1 systems.
The cluster contains five quad-core Intel Core i7 machines and 25 dual-core Core i5 models. All but two units, which date to 2014, were made in 2012. That configuration provides 70 cores, although only 64 were active in the most recent tests after one node went offline.
The museum previously reported 1.5 teraflops with all 70 cores running. Both results came from a custom Python matrix-multiplication script, so the figures reflect performance on that test rather than across a range of applications.
A master Mac mini in the exhibit's control terminal coordinates the other machines. The team chose macOS Mojave 10.14 instead of Linux, using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) to handle communication between nodes.

articles.title: Kontrollverlust berechenbar: Wenn lokale Sprachmodelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
articles.summary:
Physiker finden mathematische Formel: Wann lokale KI-Modelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
Die Nutzung von Sprachmodellen direkt auf Endgeräten wie Smartphones oder Tablets nimmt branchenübergreifend zu. Da diese sogenannten Edge-KI-Modelle lokal und ohne Cloud-Anbindung arbeiten, fehlen ihnen herkömmliche nachgeschaltete Sicherheitsfilter, sogenannte Guardrails.
Das birgt Risiken für Anwender:innen, die auf Offline-Modelle angewiesen sind, etwa im medizinischen, juristischen oder militärischen Sektor. Zwei Physiker der US-amerikanischen George Washington University wollen solche Risiken nun mit einer mathematischen Formel besser abschätzen.
In einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Patterns veröffentlichten Studie präsentieren Neil F. Johnson und Frank Yingjie Huo eine Gleichung, die berechnen soll, wann ein Sprachmodell von einer angemessenen Antwort zu einer potenziell schädlichen Ausgabe kippen kann.

articles.title: Inside AvisLoader: A Windows Malware Loader Built to Resist Disruption
articles.summary:
Varonis Threat Labs recently discovered AvisLoader, a new Windows loader named after the Latin word for bird. We found it on an exposed staging server alongside a ClickFix lure, supporting tools, and its Command Center.
The attack starts with a familiar ClickFix lure. A page posing as a document-signing request asks visitors to copy and run an attacker-supplied command on their machine.
The more interesting part is how AvisLoader stays connected. It communicates via Tox, an encrypted peer-to-peer (P2P) messaging network that carries commands and additional payloads from the operator.
That setup makes traditional domain-based takedowns harder. The command-and-control (C2) channel does not depend on a fixed domain or server address, and operators can keep the same identity when moving to another server.
The seller references this in a cybercrime forum listing, claiming the controller can be moved by copying its Tox save file, with clients following without the need for a domain.
In this post, we look at how AvisLoader works, the MITRE ATT&CK techniques it uses, and the indicators security teams can use to detect it.
Delivery through ClickFix and Cloudflare
The specific ClickFix lure we found alongside AvisLoader was hosted on Cloudflare Workers and made to look like a DocuSign signing request.

articles.summary:
Kenya’s central bank is seeking powers to take over struggling payment companies and sell their businesses, expanding the regulator’s role in protecting customer money when providers run into trouble.
The draft National Payment System Bill, 2026, would allow the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to intervene when a provider fails to meet its obligations to customers or other financial institutions, breaches regulatory requirements, or threatens financial stability.
The measures could put CBK at the centre of resolving failures in an industry where customers rely on private companies to hold and move their money. It could force service providers and their investors to surrender control of a troubled business before it reaches liquidation, with CBK deciding who runs it and appointing a statutory manager to sell it.
“The Central Bank may intervene in the management of a payment service provider or a payment system operator where … the payment service provider or payment system operator fails to meet its obligations to customers,” the draft bill states.
A company that fails to comply with a regulatory directive could also face action, while CBK could intervene during a crisis to protect financial stability and public confidence.

Build-or-buy is usually framed as an engineering trade-off, where developer time is weighed against integration and migration overhead, and control against the maintenance burden of a bespoke build. When we put together the 2026 Future of Platform Engineering report, we weren’t trying to settle the trade-off; we were trying to find out whether platform feature-sourcing decisions revealed anything about the platform team. It turns out it does. Across responses from 379 platform professionals, we found that teams predominantly building from scratch are less likely to have a clear strategy in place and to meet fewer of their platform goals.
This question has changed considerably with AI. Agents have made building easier than ever; an internal tool that once took months to build can now be put together in a day. But AI removes the effort of writing code, not the work of owning it. The maintenance, upgrades, and governance that come with a scratch-built feature remain, while the volume of change moving through the pipeline increases. That makes build-versus-buy a sharper strategic question than ever.

articles.title: CRA & Chip Design: The New Compliance Standard - EE Times
articles.summary:
Europe’s Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) will soon require chipmakers to prove their silicon is secure. The tools to produce that proof already exist, but they were built for a different purpose.
Europe goes first, again
On Sept. 11, the first operational part of the EU’s Cyber Resilience Act went live. From that day, any company selling a product with digital elements in Europe must flag actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents within 24 hours, with a fuller report within 72 hours, through a new reporting platform run by the EU’s cybersecurity agency, ENISA. The duty covers products already on the market, including ones shipped years ago. The rest of the law, the part that defines how products must be designed and assessed, applies from December 2027.
Europe is not the only one moving. Japan has set the rules for a new scheme that rates the security of companies in its supply chains, and the U.S. is set to require connected consumer devices bought by federal agencies to carry its Cyber Trust Mark label from January 2027. These are softer instruments, though: a voluntary rating, a label, a procurement rule. The CRA is binding law, with CE marking, fines, and a reporting clock, and it applies to anyone who sells into Europe, wherever they are based. As usual, the EU leads in regulation, for good and for bad.

According to court documents, YMCO allowed cybercriminals to conceal the theft of money from the bank accounts of US companies and transfer it abroad, primarily to Eastern European countries.
In exchange for the money laundering services, the cybercriminals paid YMCO a percentage of the stolen funds.
YMCO is estimated to have recruited more than 15,000 US residents as money mules, and to have laundered at least $10 million stolen from over 750 US bank accounts.
The organization deceived the money mules into believing they were making genuine transfers for legitimate companies.

Instead, the money mules withdrew stolen proceeds and wired them to YMCO conspirators out of the country, and never received payment for these services.

The restrictions would cover test labs and certification bodies in countries that deny reciprocal treatment to their US counterparts. Chairman Brendan Carr says fewer than 4% of electronic devices are tested in American labs.
If this all sounds familiar, there's a reason. In May 2025, the FCC initially targeted labs owned, controlled, or directed by blacklisted companies and foreign adversary governments. There was also a separate proposal to extend restrictions to every lab in China.
In April 2026, the FCC voted to advance broader restrictions and seek public comment. The latest action would turn that proposal into adopted rules, assuming commissioners approve the draft, with a transition ending December 1, 2028.
Compared with the original 2025 restrictions, the broader proposal focuses on where the testing happens. Under the draft, recognition would be limited to labs in the US or economies with reciprocal recognition agreements. That means a Western company operating a lab in mainland China would still be affected.

The takeaway: A Canadian software engineer who built a camera to identify police cars says two officers came to his home to ask why he was tracking them. They were concerned that repeated observations could expose their routines – the same information that makes searchable vehicle records useful to police and troubling to people being watched.
Anthony Sistilli described Peel Regional Police's visit last month in a YouTube video that he recently posted. His project uses automatic license plate recognition, or ALPR – the technology police use to record passing vehicles and search for them later. But Sistilli designed his camera to pick out police vehicles rather than collect plates from all traffic.
Sistilli built the prototype with a $180 camera and used AI coding tools to develop its software. The first version struggled to process 4K footage while identifying vehicles and reading their license plates. He lowered the resolution and split the work into two stages: first detect a police car, then try to read its plate.
That change reduced the amount of footage the plate-recognition software had to examine. It also made vehicle classification a prerequisite for capturing license plate data. The system would attempt a read only after deciding that a vehicle was a police car.

articles.title: Canonical Websites Disrupted in Second DDoS Attack This Year
articles.summary:
Canonical’s websites were disrupted last week by a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack, months after a larger attack hit the Ubuntu maker’s infrastructure.
The company confirmed the attack on October 8 in a post on the Ubuntu Discourse forum. “Canonical’s websites are under a sustained distributed denial of service attack,” the company said, adding that some services might not be reachable at times.
The disruption was limited to Canonical’s primary web properties, OMG! Ubuntu reported. These included ubuntu.com, canonical.com, the Ubuntu blog and developer site, and Ubuntu’s security advisory pages and API.
Developer-facing services such as Launchpad and the Snap Store did not appear to be affected.
Canonical said on October 9 that its team was still bringing affected services back, though most were accessible again. OMG! Ubuntu put the total downtime at a little over four hours.
The company has not publicly shared information on the size or origin of the cyberattack. No one appears to have taken credit for the DDoS attack.
Canonical was hit by a more disruptive attack in late April. Launchpad and the Snap Store were among the services taken down, and some users could not install Ubuntu updates. The company described that incident as a “sustained, cross-border attack.”
A hacktivist group calling itself The Islamic Cyber Resistance in Iraq – 313 Team claimed responsibility for that attack. It’s unclear whether the two incidents are connected.

articles.summary:
C’est la question qui revient le plus souvent depuis la révélation de l’incident cyber qui a frappé plusieurs enseignes de la grande distribution.
Petit rappel des faits. Dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre 2026, des pirates ont pris la main sur des systèmes de régulation frigorifique Danfoss installés dans de nombreux supermarchés français.
Cette manœuvre leur a permis d’imposer un dégivrage continu, avec une consigne de 50 degrés, dans des centaines de supermarchés en France. Intermarché, Leclerc et Super U sont notamment touchés.
Sur les réseaux sociaux, beaucoup d’internautes se sont alors demandé comment un congélateur de supermarché pouvait être piraté depuis l’extérieur du magasin.

Ledger wallets are physical devices designed to securely store the private keys that control cryptocurrency assets and authorize transactions.

The next day, the company confirmed hardware tampering on at least one device, though it’s still unclear exactly how or when the devices were tampered with.
"Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger is reaching out to impacted users as part of the ongoing investigation," Ledger said.
The crypto wallet maker also noted that it was working with authorities to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.

Publicado na revista Nature Cities, o trabalho mostra diferenças significativas entre as localidades analisadas. A Cidade do México registrou os casos mais rápidos de afundamento em áreas específicas, enquanto cidades da Ásia apresentaram algumas das maiores taxas medianas em escala municipal. O fenômeno pode danificar edifícios e sistemas de infraestrutura, além de aumentar os riscos de inundação.
Cidade do México tem áreas com afundamento acelerado
A subsidência do solo, nome dado ao processo gradual de rebaixamento do terreno, pode comprometer construções, fundações e sistemas de drenagem e esgoto. Apesar desses riscos, ainda existem limitações no conhecimento sobre a dinâmica do fenômeno, o que dificulta identificar os locais que precisam de intervenções urgentes.
Na Cidade do México, algumas áreas apresentaram uma taxa de afundamento de aproximadamente 217 milímetros por ano, o equivalente a 21,7 centímetros anuais. Apesar desse resultado localizado, a mediana da taxa de afundamento considerando a cidade foi de 8 milímetros por ano.
Outra cidade mexicana, Torreón, registrou um afundamento de cerca de 17 milímetros anuais.

articles.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary:
A critical vulnerability in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin is being exploited in the wild, according to WordPress security company Patchstack.
The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-85097 and it has a CVSS score of 9.8. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit it to upload arbitrary files and execute malicious code.
This can allow threat actors to take full control of the targeted WordPress websites.
The security hole was patched with the release of version 3.1.8.10. Versions 3.1.8.9 and earlier are affected.
Patchstack started seeing in-the-wild exploitation attempts on October 7.
Bricksforge is a commercial add-on for the Bricks visual site builder that layers extra tools onto WordPress sites, such as custom forms, animations, an email designer, and admin-area pages. Patchstack reported that it’s used by roughly 6,000 websites.
“Two clusters stand out in our telemetry,” Patchstack explained. “In the first, 44 IPs sent 56 requests with identical payloads within seconds of each other. In the second, three IPs tested 25 variations of PHP extensions and encodings against the same temporary file.”
The company added, “Both patterns point to automated exploitation over rotating proxies or distributed infrastructure. They do not, on their own, attribute the activity to a single threat actor.”
It’s not uncommon for threat actors to target WordPress vulnerabilities shortly after patches are released, including plugin flaws and weaknesses affecting WordPress itself.

Cómo funciona el método de etiquetado triple en WhatsApp
La base del sistema está en la función de búsqueda por texto exacto que ofrece WhatsApp. Esa herramienta, pensada originalmente para rastrear conversaciones, se convierte aquí en un motor de clasificación cuando se combina con hashtags escritos de forma constante.

La primera responde a la pregunta de dónde pertenece el contenido, con hashtags como #Trabajo, #Estudios, #Recetas, #Finanzas u #Hogar. La segunda precisa qué tipo de recurso es, mediante etiquetas como #Video, #PDF, #Curso o #Herramienta.

‘I did it all with the help of AI’: a driver used ChatGPT to help him with a three-year parking ticket dispute — and won
Who needs a lawyer when you've got ChatGPT?
- Essex man Rafal Gorfal used ChatGPT to help him win a legal dispute over a parking ticket fine
- He fed the AI the letters he received from debt collectors, and it told him what to say and where to go
- The fine was dropped just weeks before his scheduled court appearance
People use AI chatbots like ChatGPT for all manner of things, but have you ever used AI to evade a parking ticket fine before? This man did, and he went on to win a three-year-long legal battle.
Rafal Gorfal, who’s originally from Essex, was fined back in August 2023 for not paying fast enough in a Newquay pay-and-display car park. Gorfal said that when he arrived at the payment machine he had to wait in a long queue, only to learn that the machine was cash-only, to which he had no choice but to download the RingGo and pay with his phone — delaying his payment further.
Two weeks later, he was presented with a £100 fine that said he didn’t pay for a ticket until 16 minutes after entering the car park, which was delayed due to the long queue and the time it took Gorfal to set up an online account to pay.
A long three years

articles.title: GPUs on Kubernetes are bring-your-own-everything, starting with the bill
articles.summary:
GPUs on Kubernetes are bring-your-own-everything, starting with the bill
If you run a Kubernetes platform, you’ve probably got at least one Grafana dashboard for resource visibility on your workloads. It shows what a container asked for versus what it used, making it relatively easy to point at the deployment that requested four cores and is only using half of one. If you break it down by namespace you get a rough idea which team is consuming what, which is what teams have been doing for CPU and memory for years and it mostly works.
Then people started putting workloads on GPUs and a lot of what we assumed would carry over didn’t. Almost every piece of visibility you take for granted on CPU and memory, GPUs make you build yourself. Your own metrics, your own accuracy, your own rules for splitting the bill. Which is what stings the most, since the GPU is the most expensive line on the bill.
Bring your own metrics
With CPU and memory, the kernel already tracks usage per container for you, so getting a per-pod number is basically free. GPUs on the other hand, don’t give you that. The tool everybody starts with, NVIDIA’s DCGM exporter, reports at the physical device level by default. This is fine when one pod has a GPU to itself, but the second you start sharing a GPU across pods, with time-slicing or MPS, DCGM gives every pod sharing that GPU the same value. So if three pods are sharing one GPU, all three look like they’re using the whole thing, and when you add it up you get 30…

This startup's electric farm machine can help ease India’s labour shortage
Balisto Agritech's battery-powered machine can handle several farm jobs on a single platform, with an autonomous version now in development.
Farm work is labour-intensive, and fewer young people want to do it. On small plots, farmers often need different machines for different jobs. With diesel expensive, many continue to depend on manual labour and bullocks.
Mumbai-based Balisto Agritech, founded in 2024, is addressing this with the Balisto 130 Pro, an electric, multi-purpose farm machine. Designed to work across the crop cycle, it reduces the need for farmers to rely on a combination of labour, bullocks, and multiple diesel-powered machines.
The startup was founded by IIT Bombay alumni Aishwarya Ramakrishnan and Kedar Gokhale, who later worked together at Boston Consulting Group.
Ramakrishnan, who also has an MBA from Harvard Business School, worked at the Mahindra Group, first in the Chairman’s Office and later setting up the group’s agritech venture, Krish-e. Gokhale ran his own agritech startup, Truce, before becoming vice president of operations at Swiggy, where he led its delivery fleet across India.
Balisto took 18 to 20 months to move from prototype to commercial rollout. Along the way, it sold an initial batch to paying farmers to gather feedback.

articles.title: Votre PC Windows pourrait être privé de mise à jour en 2027, mais il y a un moyen d'éviter ça
articles.summary:
À partir du 17 mai ou du 19 juin 2027 (selon la version), votre PC sous Windows pourrait ne plus pouvoir se mettre à jour. Cela concerne les machines qui n’auront pas reçu les nouveaux certificats de Windows Update. Le moyen le plus facile d’éviter cette infortune : mettre à jour votre ordinateur.
Windows Update a besoin d’un certificat pour continuer à mettre à jour votre PC Windows
Windows Update utilise des certificats numériques pour vérifier qu’un PC communique bien avec les serveurs officiels de Microsoft. Cependant, certains d’entre eux doivent expirer le 17 mai 2027 et le 19 juin 2027, comme l’a rappelé le blog de Microsoft dédié aux administrateurs réseau. Leurs remplaçants sont bien intégrés aux mises à jour mensuelles de Windows : un appareil qui reçoit les correctifs nécessaires à temps devrait donc conserver l’accès à Windows Update.
Rassurez-vous, si les certificats de votre ordinateur ne sont pas renouvelés, vous pourrez quand même l’utiliser. Mais il ne pourra plus recevoir les mises à jour de sécurité, les correctifs de fiabilité et autres mises à jours de Windows proposés via Windows Update. Plus le temps avancera, plus le risque d’être visé par une vulnérabilité nouvellement découverte augmentera. Dans le cas où Windows Update ne proposerait pas le correctif, Microsoft précise qu’il peut être téléchargé depuis le Catalogue Microsoft Update.

articles.summary:
A principio de los años 80, los contables vieron amenazados sus puestos de trabajo por la llegada de una nueva herramienta que lo cambiaría todo: la hoja de cálculo. El trabajo que un empleado antes hacía a mano en un día, con la nueva herramienta salía en segundos. Los departamentos de cálculo manual desaparecieron, pero los contables, que parecían los siguientes en extinguirse, se quedaron desarrollando otros roles.
Casi medio siglo después, la IA reabre aquel miedo, y esta vez la amenaza apunta a todo el mercado laboral a la vez. Un informe de McKinsey ha intentado medir ese impacto y sus conclusiones nos llevan a los mismos resultados que ya descubrieron los contables al principio de la era informática.
Las cuentas salen a favor. McKinsey calcula que, hasta 2035, la automatización que permitirá la IA restará una demanda equivalente a 36 millones de empleos solo en EEUU. Esa cifra es una equivalencia en horas de trabajo que ya no harán falta debido al ahorro de tiempo que proporciona esa automatización, no a personas despedidas.

articles.title: California sues major 3D-printing filament maker over claims it deliberately catered to ghost gun enthusiasts
articles.summary:
A hot potato: California's long-running battle against 3D-printed guns has just seen San Diego County, acting on behalf of the state, sue Polymaker LLC, one of the world's largest 3D-printing filament manufacturers. The lawsuit claims that Polymaker intentionally markets and sells its filament to Californians with the express purpose of creating illegal ghost guns.
The complaint, which was filed on October 5 in San Diego County Superior Court, acknowledges that 3D printing filament is not illegal. However, it alleges that Polymaker intentionally marketed its product toward ghost gun aficionados so they could turn its filament into a regulated "firearm precursor part."
California law describes a firearm precursor part as including an article marketed or sold to the public to become or be used as the frame or receiver of a functional firearm once completed, assembled or converted.
The complaint adds that Polymaker monetized the ghost gun community by supporting and hiring Sean Aranda, also known as The 3D Print General. After he was banned from YouTube in 2023 over firearm policy violations, Polymaker offered him a job as Head of Customer Experience. He is now a Senior Technical Account Manager at the company.
The suit alleges that hiring Aranda was part of Polymaker's effort to target 3D-printed gun enthusiasts.
The complaint also points to affiliate payments and firearm-themed products as evidence that the company actively cultivated this particular market for its filament.

articles.summary:
Citroën dévoile sa nouvelle 2CV électrique pour défier Renault et casser les prix
Présentée au Mondial de l’Automobile à Paris, la nouvelle Citroën 2CV électrique ressuscite la célèbre icône des années 1950, avec toujours un prix promis sous la barre des 15 000 euros dès 2028.
Alors que Renault cartonne en restylant d’anciens modèles en versions électriques (R5, R4, Twingo…), Stellantis tente enfin l’aventure en officialisant sa Citroën 2CV électrique. Une nouvelle citadine néo-rétro qui a tous les codes de son aînée de 1948 couplés à une bonne dose de modernité. La volonté du groupe est aussi de cibler les petits budgets en tablant sur un tarif ultra-concurrentiel. Il faudra cependant attendre 2028 pour qu’elle goûte à nos routes.
Le minimalisme de la 2CV électrique a tout pour réussir, mais il faudra attendre 2028
La 2CV électrique mise sans grande surprise sur un design connu de tous, avec une silhouette qui conserve la ligne en double arc emblématique de la Deuche originelle. The ecologist revealing the invisible networks that revive rainforests
Massive tree-planting programs lead to unhealthy monocrop plantations. Daisy Dent aims to help forests rebuild themselves.
In a research station in central Panama, you can walk through a century of forest time, watching scrubby plots of adolescent trees give way to cathedral-like canopies of mature growth. Forest ecologist Daisy Dent, a senior scientist at ETH Zurich, oversees this sequence of plots across the Barro Colorado Nature Monument, some of which date as far back as the 19th century. Not one of the trees she surveys was planted by human hands. She maps, measures, and tracks each trunk that emerges, revealing how waves of tree life rise from bare earth.
Tropical forests like these are our planet’s biggest terrestrial carbon sink, accounting for around 40% of carbon stored on land. As part of an international network of researchers, Dent is deciphering the networks of animal and plant interactions that enable some forests to recover after destruction. The goal is a low-cost, high-impact alternative to typical carbon-crediting schemes, which plant huge areas with a single species of tree. For over a decade, her research has built a body of evidence that such large “monocrop” programs could be expensive mistakes—and that more resilient forests can rebound naturally in just a few decades, re-creating ecosystems that suck up vast quantities of carbon dioxide.

articles.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
articles.summary:
GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending. The release moves GitLab's agents beyond individual prompts and predefined flows, while keeping their actions within the permissions and approval rules already used by a project.
The new /goal command in GitLab Duo CLI, now in public beta, accepts an open-ended objective and continues working until it completes the task or reaches an iteration limit. One model implements the changes while a separate model checks progress against the stated goal. A developer can stop the run, change the goal, or redirect the agent. The work runs locally and retains the project's existing context and controls.
"This release takes agentic automation from something individual developers use to something an organization can scale at speed and under the controls already in place."
Manav Khurana, GitLab
GitLab's use of the word "verified" has a specific meaning here. The second model judges whether the result meets the natural-language goal; this is not formal verification of the code. The command can report work that it could not resolve, and the iteration limit prevents it from continuing indefinitely. Africa’s push to connect one billion people by 2030 faces a bigger challenge than network coverage: getting the hundreds of millions already within reach of a signal to use the internet meaningfully.
In 2025, about 550 million Africans, or 36% of the continent’s population, used the internet, up from 16% in 2015. That remains far below the global internet usage rate of 74%, underscoring the gap Africa must close to meet its regional digital inclusion goals. But the challenge is not simply extending network coverage. Most Africans who remain offline already live within reach of a mobile broadband signal, pointing to barriers such as device affordability, digital skills, and the perceived value of going online.
About 906 million Africans live in areas covered by mobile broadband but do not use mobile internet, according to a joint report by the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa and GSMA Intelligence. Another 122 million live in areas without last-mile mobile or fixed connectivity.
That distinction matters because Africa’s connectivity gap is no longer simply a story about towers, fibre, and coverage. It is increasingly about whether people can afford a device, see a reason to go online, trust digital services, or use them in ways that improve their lives.
Ghana, Egypt, and Niger illustrate three versions of that problem.

Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. Das Urteil vom 24. Juli 2026 (Az. 1 HK O 1352/25) wurde in der vergangenen Woche veröffentlicht und ist noch nicht rechtskräftig.

En Francia, esto ya ha ocurrido durante 800 horas este año, pero otros países como Suecia, Países Bajos o España también están registrando periodos negativos. ¿Por qué está ocurriendo y qué consecuencias tiene para el sistema eléctrico?

Le Réseau de Transport d’Électricité (RTE) explica en su página web que en el mercado mayorista de electricidad los proveedores compran electricidad a un precio calculado, en este caso cada cuarto de hora, según la oferta y la demanda. A ese precio se le conoce como precio spot y, a nivel europeo, este sistema sigue un modelo de precios marginales. Esto significa que el precio de la última central eléctrica que se utiliza para abastecer la demanda es el que determina el precio para todas las demás.
Cuando la producción supera al consumo y no hay suficiente flexibilidad para absorber el excedente, el precio mayorista del megavatio-hora puede caer por debajo de cero. A hot potato: AI has been helping police forces across the US over the last few years, for better and for worse. The latest use of the technology allows law enforcement to input an interior photo of a home and have the AI figure out the location, though there are some caveats.
The tool, which is called Raven, is being used by the Los Angeles Police Department and Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office (MDSO), reports 404 Media. Made by a company called Graylark Technologies, Raven had been called GeoSpy before its new home-identification features were added.
The limitation is that Raven can't just identify any home in the world solely from an interior photo. Its abilities appear limited to certain properties. Graylark CEO Daniel Heinen demonstrated its power in a LinkedIn post, showing how a regional search can be carried out on something as simple as a photo of a washing machine and dryer.
While Heinen doesn't mention it in the post, 404 Media confirmed that the language generated in the results directly quotes listings on Airbnb and short-term rental site Vrbo.
It's noted that this isn't a simple reverse image search. Raven picks out distinctive details in a photo and uses them to find likely matches from the same property on sites such as Airbnb, even when the images differ.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped how the world works, and African AI startups, venture capital and tech ecosystems are no exception. The technology is evolving so fast that many investors are still working out how to evaluate AI startups, let alone how to fund them.
Over the past six months, this column has spoken to African investors across regions, sectors, and funding stages about where AI creates genuine value, where it falls short, and what merits institutional capital.
They are Babacar Seck, founder of Askya Investment Partners; Eloho Omame, partner at TLcom Capital; Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica; Magnifique Ishimwe, fund manager at the Development Bank of Rwanda; Husein Merchant, investment officer at Village Capital; and Benjamin Toulouze, head of corporate venture capital at AXIAN Investment.
When we asked them what makes an AI startup fundable, they mostly described something an AI model itself cannot supply. articles.title: Unerwartetes Wetterphänomen: Wie sich auf dem Mars eine 1.800 Kilometer lange Wolke formt
articles.summary:
Mars-Rätsel gelöst: Gigantische Wolke am Vulkan Arsia Mons entsteht völlig ohne Staub
Die europäische Weltraumorganisation Esa hat neue Daten zur sogenannten Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud veröffentlicht. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entsteht dieses langgestreckte Gebilde durch einen bisher in planetaren Atmosphären nicht beobachteten Mechanismus. Dieser physikalische Prozess, die sogenannte homogene Keimbildung, vollzieht sich gänzlich ohne die Anwesenheit von Kondensationskernen wie Staub oder Schmutzpartikeln.
Dabei galt in der meteorologischen Forschung bislang ein fester Grundsatz: Wasserdampf benötigt zwingend Staub oder andere winzige Partikel, um zu kondensieren. Da die Atmosphäre des Mars extrem staubig ist, nahmen bisherige Klimamodelle diesen Vorgang stets als alleinigen Standardmechanismus an.
Die aktuellen Computersimulationen eines Forschungsteams um Jorge Hernández-Bernal und Franck Forget von der französischen Sorbonne Université in Paris widerlegen dies nun. Sie zeigen, dass diese etablierte Grundannahme für die lange Arsia-Mons-Wolke schlichtweg nicht gilt.
Wie der Mars-Vulkan das Wetter extrem beschleunigt
Der rund 20 Kilometer hohe Vulkan Arsia Mons wirkt auf den Marswind wie eine gigantische Rampe. Wenn die Luftströmungen auf das massive Hindernis treffen, werden sie als atmosphärische Wellen mit hoher Geschwindigkeit nach oben gedrückt. articles.title: Frigos piratés dans les supermarchés : la faille était connue, mais le matériel trop vieux ou pas mis à jour — Frandroid

Danfoss, le fabricant danois dont les régulateurs pilotent le froid de nombreux supermarchés, a donné ses premières explications ce lundi 12 octobre. Ses systèmes ont été piratés dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, quand les frigos d’Intermarché, Super U et Leclerc sont montés jusqu’à 50 °C, provoquant un immense gâchis alimentaire. Dans une déclaration relayée par FrenchBreaches, le groupe reconnaît des incidents en France sur « un nombre limité » de ses systèmes, sans donner de chiffre. Il assure que la plupart des appareils touchés étaient trop vieux pour recevoir des correctifs de sécurité, ou n’avaient pas été mis à jour.
Les pirates auraient détourné le dégivrage, ce cycle qui coupe le froid quelques minutes pour faire fondre le givre dans les meubles frigorifiques. Ils l’auraient forcé avec des consignes allant jusqu’à 50 °C. Des centaines de magasins Intermarché, Super U et Leclerc ont ainsi vu leur chaîne du froid ruinée.
Des appareils en fin de vie depuis des années
Danfoss cite deux modèles en particulier, l’AK-SM800 et l’AK-SC355. Il s’agit de centrales de supervision : depuis un seul écran, souvent accessible à distance, elles règlent les températures, les alarmes et les horaires de tous les meubles frigorifiques d’un magasin. Le premier a été déclaré en fin de vie en 2021, le second retiré du catalogue en 2016. Aucun des deux ne reçoit plus de mise à jour de sécurité.

El baile de las cifras.
